newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DASA sees fewer 1996 job losses - paper.
newsitem.headline: German DASA sees fewer 1996 job losses - paper.

text.p: Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa) is expecting to make around 1,000 fewer redundancies in 1996 than originally expected as a result of strong orders and earlier cost-cutting, a German newspaper said on Saturday.

Boersen-Zeitung, quoting from an interview with Dasa chairman Manfred Bischoff, said strong aircraft orders meant around 470 jobs could now be saved, while a similar number would be spared after cost improvements suggested by the workforce.
Bischoff was further quoted as saying that strong demand in the civilian sector had offset the effect of lower government spending on the Daimler unit's revenues.

"We remain in line with our expectations," Bischoff was quoted as saying. A report by the company earlier this year foresaw a loss of around 780 million marks ($510 million) at the operating level compared with a 2.7 billion mark loss in 1995, the paper said.
Bischoff was further quoted as saying the recent strength of the dollar was having a positive but unquantifiable effect on the group's business.
"We have learnt to live with the dollar at 1.50 to the mark," he said. The dollar traded in New York late on Friday at 1.53 to the German currency.
